summary: --venv runs tests in an ansible-test-managed Python virtual environment with requirements installed automatically; use it for unit and integration tests when --docker and --remote aren't available.
questions: Can I run ansible-test without Docker?
Does --venv install test dependencies for me?

answer_card.title: Run ansible-test in a virtualenv
answer_card.answer_md: When you can't use `--docker` or `--remote`, use `--venv`. ansible-test creates and manages a Python virtual environment and installs the requirements automatically before running unit or integration tests.
